_: GutLog v3.18.0, browser side: the Watch card and the medicines banner in
test_ui_now.py. Four of the six are behaviour v3.17.0 did not have -- it
drew 'no data' over a metric that had arrived with a six-day median, it
drew a tile for load_hours that held nothing at all, and it painted the
medicines banner amber for housekeeping every morning.
Two guard the other direction and cannot fail on a version change, so
each is broken on purpose in a copy of the current app:
smallmed  gives the new median figure 12px type, and the card's
existing 14px floor has to catch it. That is what discharges
'no sub-14px type in anything new' for this change: the floor
is now shown to be measuring the new element and not merely
neverred  makes the banner neutral even with a RED, so the assertion
that it still shouts when it should has been seen failing.
Two assertions in the block are deliberately NOT declared, because they
are fixture self-checks rather than claims about the app: 'the sparse
stub actually served /api/watch' and 'the medicines banner is stubbed
and drawn'. Both exist so that a bypassed route fails loudly instead of
leaving the assertions below testing the live handler.

assertions.name: a metric with no reading today shows its median instead of an absence
the median tile names the window the median came from
a tile that holds nothing is not drawn at all
with no RED the banner is neutral, not an alert
nothing inside the card is smaller than 14px

mutation.why: type the new median figure at 12px and see the card's 14px floor catch it

assertions.name: with a RED the banner is an alert and names it

mutation.why: make the banner neutral even when RxGuard has a RED, and see the assertion catch it
